entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

input.summary: Baseline run findings for bid entry
input.message:
Three findings from a fresh sandbox run of unchanged v1 (run_d4deebd2d3a2d429, 713 s, 105 model calls, quality 10) that belong to your part; please fold them in.
1. TAN lookup: 4 of 6 lookups stopped at the 8-request limit (each 16 to 22 s), the two that worked took 2 and 4 requests. One of them logged a `fill` action error with a 5 s timeout in the mailbox. The bid worker asked for a TAN six times, so several TANs were invalidated. Find the cause from your own traces (where the mailbox tab stands, what the worker does with its 8 requests) and fix that; the lookup should start from a known state each time.
2. The bid form took 428 s before the first TAN request, with every position omitted. Model answering time summed to 933 s over the run against 243 s of GPU queueing, i.e. about 9 s of answering per call: the bid worker runs with thinking on (`thinking=True` in submit.py). Measure thinking off for the form-filling steps (v1's fastest runs were 87 to 105 s) and keep thinking on only where a decision needs it, if anywhere. Another engineer is adding an output-token cap in llm.py; do not edit llm.py yourself.
3. After the platform accepted the answer, the agent kept calling the model and crashed with a 401 "finished or expired run token" traceback. Once the site confirms the submission the run is over: return and exit cleanly (catch model HTTP errors after a confirmed submission, and make sure nothing else is awaited after it).
Also: `tzdata` is now a dependency in agent/pyproject.toml (I added it; run `uv sync` in agent/ if your venv complains). `build_plan` in agent/bidplan.py is implemented and tested now, so your end-to-end runs get a real plan as soon as research returns findings.

content.text:
The baseline test run you asked for is done and committed (`58af24c`): quality 10 again, but slow and expensive compared with the same code earlier today.

## Test run `run_d4deebd2d3a2d429` (unchanged v1)

| | This run | v1's fastest run today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quality | 10 | 10 |
| Time | 11.9 min | 87 s |
| Model calls | 105 | 27 |
| Cost | $0.069 | $0.010 |

- **The bid form took 428 s before the first TAN request,** with every position omitted. Model answering summed to 933 s, about 9 s per call, because the bid worker runs with thinking on.
- **Four of six TAN lookups stopped at their 8-request limit.** Each new TAN request invalidates the previous one, so the agent went round six times.
- **The agent crashed after the answer was accepted.** It kept calling the model and ended in a 401 traceback; the score was unaffected.
- **v1's run time is not stable.** The same code ranged from 87 s to 11.9 minutes today, so a single run says little.

## Changes I'd suggest (already passed to the bid-entry agent)
1. Measure thinking off for the form-filling steps and keep it on only where a decision needs it.
2. Fix the cause of the TAN lookup running out of requests, not only raise the limit.
3. Exit cleanly once the site confirms the submission.

## Idea taken from a teammate's line
The teammate's research run had a helper that follows a "next page" control and keeps all pages. The research agent is building our version of that as a tool that also works inside frames.

## Build status
- **Plan and parsing: done.** `build_plan` and the parsers are implemented; the full suite of 129 tests passed in that agent's run. I added the `tzdata` dependency it flagged, so named timezones (the Q&A dates) parse in the sandbox.
- **Research workers: still running.**
- **Orchestration and bid entry: still running.**

One behaviour differs from what I asked for: in a no_bid plan an unconditional discount approval keeps its percent instead of going to 0. That follows the existing tested rule in `calc.py`, and I'm leaving it as is.

Next is integration when the two remaining agents report: full test suite, a local end-to-end run, then the first v2 sandbox run. What you could change before then: say now if you'd rather the first v2 sandbox run waits for your go, otherwise I start it as soon as a local run ends with a signed bid that has positions filled.

"""
What the research workers bring back: one typed record per kind of fact, as the pages show it.

Values stay verbatim strings (a worker's result is checked against the pages it saw, so nothing may be reformatted
on the way). Each record says how its numbers and dates are written where the page states it; `parse.py` turns them
into numbers and times, and `bidplan.py` applies the bid rules through `calc.py`. A field the worker could not
establish is left empty: an empty field omits the position, it is never guessed.
"""
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

NumberFormat = Literal["de", "en", ""]  # "1.234,56" or "1,234.56"; "" when the page does not say
DateOrder = Literal["dmy", "mdy", "ymd", ""]  # day-first, month-first or ISO; "" when the page does not say


class Dated(BaseModel):
    """When a record was issued. Prefer a machine-readable timestamp the page carries (e.g. datetime=...)."""
    date: str = Field(default="", description="Date or timestamp exactly as shown; the ISO one if the page has it")
    date_order: DateOrder = Field(default="", description="Order of day and month the page states for this date")
    timezone: str = Field(default="", description="Timezone or UTC offset the page states for it, as shown")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tender


class TenderPosition(BaseModel):
    position: str = Field(description="Position number exactly as the bill of quantities writes it")
    quantity: str = Field(description="Tender quantity as shown")
    unit: str = Field(description="Unit as shown (pieces or sets)")
    requirement: str = Field(default="", description="The specification requirement this position refers to")
    number_format: NumberFormat = ""


class QuantityChange(Dated):
    """A bidder Q&A answer that sets a new quantity for one position."""
    answer: str = Field(description="Number of the Q&A answer")
    position: str
    quantity: str
    unit: str = ""
    number_format: NumberFormat = ""


class Withdrawal(Dated):
    """A Q&A answer that withdraws an earlier answer."""
    answer: str = Field(description="Number of the withdrawing answer")
    withdraws: str = Field(description="Number of the answer it withdraws")


class Amendment(Dated):
    """A Q&A answer that changes named attributes of one requirement in one specification revision."""
    answer: str
    revision: str
    requirement: str
    attributes: dict[str, str] = Field(description="Only the attributes it names (bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, "
                                                   "certification), each value as shown")
    number_format: NumberFormat = ""


class TenderFindings(BaseModel):
    positions: list[TenderPosition] = []
    quantity_changes: list[QuantityChange] = []
    withdrawals: list[Withdrawal] = []
    amendments: list[Amendment] = []
    complete: bool = Field(default=False, description="True only if every position and every Q&A page was read")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- specification


class Requirement(BaseModel):
    requirement: str = Field(description="Requirement identifier as the specification writes it")
    bore: str = ""
    stroke: str = ""
    pressure: str = ""
    mounting: str = ""
    certification: str = ""
    catalogue_group: str = Field(default="", description="The catalogue group named for this requirement")
    pieces_per_set: str = Field(default="", description="Pieces per set, if the requirement states it")
    usable_stroke: bool = Field(default=False, description="True if the stroke is given as usable travel, to which "
                                                           "an end reserve must be added")
    reserve_key: str = Field(default="", description="The key naming the end reserve, if stated")
    number_format: NumberFormat = ""


class SpecFindings(BaseModel):
    current_revision: str = Field(default="", description="The revision the site marks as current")
    requirements: list[Requirement] = []
    complete: bool = Field(default=False, description="True only if every requirement page of that revision was read")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- ERP


class Candidate(BaseModel):
    """One material the ERP lists for a catalogue group."""
    material_number: str
    bore: str = ""
    stroke: str = ""
    pressure: str = ""
    mounting: str = ""
    certification: str = ""
    status: str = Field(default="", description="Status exactly as shown")
    active: bool | None = Field(default=None, description="True if the status means usable, False if blocked")
    number_format: NumberFormat = ""


class Scale(BaseModel):
    min_quantity: str
    price: str


class Condition(BaseModel):
    """One price condition record of a material."""
    valid_from: str
    valid_to: str = ""
    date_order: DateOrder = ""
    currency: str = ""
    fx_key: str = ""
    price_unit: str = Field(default="", description="How many pieces the price refers to, as shown")
    scales: list[Scale] = []
    number_format: NumberFormat = ""


class MaterialFacts(BaseModel):
    """Stock, lead times and prices of the material chosen for a requirement."""
    material_number: str
    free_stock: str = Field(default="", description="Unrestricted stock, not blocked or reserved stock")
    stock_lead_time_weeks: str = ""
    production_lead_time_weeks: str = ""
    conditions: list[Condition] = []
    number_format: NumberFormat = ""


class ErpFindings(BaseModel):
    requirement: str

Read in full on 2026-10-10 (challenge version 6): `llms-full.txt` (all docs), the scouting brief, announcements,
`docs/plan.md`. The repo `CLAUDE.md` already holds the 29 rules, traps and dev loop; this file holds only what it
lacks. The user asked (2026-10-10) that this understanding be kept available for every decision. Re-fetch
`https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms-full.txt` and `/v1/announcements` when a decision depends on a detail: they change.

**Scoring details**
- no_bid case splits: decision 75, tender reference 5, no positions 5, total of 0 15.
- Bid case: positions get 75 minus 5 for each extra check present (withdrawn Q&A quantity, dated metal index), so 65
  when both exist; split evenly across positions.
- Quality 100 was already reached by two teams on the public board on 2026-10-10 (best about $0.09 and 6.5 min), so
  at the top the ranking is decided by cost x time. Organizers hint at a small prize for the quickest and cheapest
  passing solution.
- Private final runs show no breakdown and mask private values in logs as `[private]`.

**Brief facts stated for every scenario (allowed in prompts)**
- Discount approvals come from `leitung@` + the bidder mailbox domain; other authorized local parts are in rule 21.
- Submission flow named in the brief: express interest, register the bidder with the company name and VAT id given
  in that run's brief, choose main bid or waiver (no_bid), configurator, prices in German number format, acknowledge
  the tender documents, TAN from webmail, confirm in a browser dialog. The displayed gross amount includes VAT and is
  not the net total.
- Exactly one submission; submitting ends the run. Going back clears later steps; unsaved entries are lost on session
  expiry. A new TAN request invalidates the previous one; a TAN is valid five minutes.
- The scenario date comes from the brief, not the wall clock; sites run on the scenario clock.

**Run logistics**
- Sandbox: 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 30 GB disk, 1280x800 screens, Python 3.12 + uv, Node 24, Rust.
- Hosted-model warm-up (1 to 8 min) happens before the clock starts; `"models": []` skips the wait, and absent means
  wait for all hosted models. After a 202 the agent has 10 s to exit.
- Test runs: docs say up to 7 running and 3 waiting per team (an announcement said 4 running; organizers adjust it).
  Keep test runs under 20 min even though 2 h is allowed.
- Announcement (2026-10-10): eligible test runs under 20 min can be promoted to the leaderboard through the same
  review. Whether a promoted test run also becomes the "latest passed submission" for the private final is not
  stated: ask the organizers before promoting.
- A platform failure (hosted model down for most of a run that ends without an answer) does not count and a scored
  run restarts once by itself.
- Own-key models outside runs: proxy at `$API/llm/<provider>/...` with header `x-atira-team-key: <personal token>`;
  in runs the provider SDK base URLs are preset and the key is a team secret. Unpriced models are refused except via
  OpenRouter.
- Request body limit to the model proxy is 32 MiB.
- Organizers ask teams to link the (private) GitHub repo; elegance is the third winner criterion, so the linked
  source is read by people.

# Plan: v2 on the v1 harness, positions scored

## Context

Our best run scores 10 of 100: v1 signs a bid with every position omitted, so only decision and tender reference
earn points. Two teams already score 100. A teammate's larger research agent is not pushed and its test run still
scored 10 (research hit its time budget without a plan), so you chose to build on v1 from `main`.

Target for the first run that counts: a signed bid in under 20 minutes with **material, quantity, lead time, base
price, final unit price, discount and total** for every position research finished, the rest omitted. Ceiling about
70 of 100 on the public scenario; the clause rules (surcharge, packaging, bonus, metal index: about 30) come after.

Measured constraint that shapes the design: a model call waits 2 to 3 s for a GPU and answers in 0.35 s, at about
$0.0004. Time and cost are both the number of sequential calls, so: narrow goals, thinking off for navigation,
workers side by side.

Work happens on branch `speed-cost`. Commits follow the working agreement below; nothing is pushed or submitted
without you asking.

## How we proceed

Seven steps. After each one I stop, show what changed and what the check returned, and wait for your go before the
next. Each step leaves the agent runnable (it still ends with a signed bid).

### Step 1: site roles and four browsers

- `agent/briefing.py`: extend `Briefing` with the siteId of the tender site, the specification site and the ERP
  (the model maps them from the brief, as it already does for `bid_site` and `mail_site`), and validate them against
  the run's access list like the existing `_from_brief` check.
- `agent/agent.json`: `"browsers": 4`. `agent/agent.py`: one `SiteSession` per site through the existing
  `browsers.more_contexts(page, 4)`, started together with `asyncio.gather`.
- Check: local run still signs the v1 bid; trace shows four sessions signed in.

### Step 2: findings and the plan (pure code, unit-tested)

- New `agent/evidence.py`: small pydantic records for what the workers return: tender position (number, quantity,
  unit, requirement reference), quantity changes and withdrawals (reuse `calc.QuantityChange`), requirement
  (bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification, catalogue group, pieces per set, usable-stroke marker),
  material candidate (attributes, status, plus `calc.Material`).
- New `agent/bidplan.py`: turns findings into per-position entries using what `calc.py` already has:
  `resolve_quantity`, `to_pieces`, `apply_amendments`, `matching_materials`, `lead_time` (with pooled demand per
  material). A position with a gap is marked "omit" with the reason; complete ones carry material, pieces, lead time.
- `agent/tests/test_bidplan.py` with invented numbers only.
- Check: `uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests` passes.

### Step 3: research workers, staged and parallel

- New `agent/research.py`, all through the existing `worker.run_worker` and `browser_tools` (grounding check stays
  on, so values must come from pages the worker saw):
  - Stage A, in parallel: a tender worker (positions with units, then the Q&A: quantity changes, withdrawals,
    scoped amendments) and a specification worker (which revision is current, then each position's requirement).
  - Stage B, as soon as a requirement is known: ERP lookups per catalogue group, several tabs in the ERP's context
    so positions run side by side (candidates, attributes, status, free stock, both lead times).
- Each worker returns typed, partial results; a position's facts are handed over as soon as they exist, so a
  cut-off never leaves the plan empty (the failure seen in the teammate's run).
- Prompts name roles and goals only: no site names, URLs, labels or values. The model picks the revision, the
  records and the matching material; `matching_materials` only cross-checks its choice.
- Time budget from the existing deadline in `agent.py`: research stops with enough left to enter positions and
  sign. Thinking on only for the "which revision / which material" decisions.
- Check: `dev/smoke.py`-style local run prints the findings per position; I compare them by eye against the sites
  (outside `agent/`, nothing stored).

### Step 3b: prices and discount

- ERP worker also reads, for the chosen material, the price conditions with validity, currency, price unit and
  quantity scales (into `calc.PriceCondition`); `calc.valid_condition` and `calc.reached_scale` pick by scenario date
  and per-position pieces.

  list of public-1 facts in `checks/` (outside `agent/`, gitignored, never packaged) and a script that compares a
  local run's findings with it, so a wrong material or quantity shows up before a sandbox run.
- `docs/plan.md` and the status paragraph of `CLAUDE.md` still describe v1. Updated when v2 passes its first run,
  not before.
- Rule-level lessons that hold for any dataset (grounding, timing, budgets) are kept apart from public-1 layout
  notes inside `docs/learned.md`, so the first kind steers prompts and the second never does.

## Added before coding (were missing)

- **Time budget inside a run**, fixed in `agent.py` from the run's `expires_at`: research hands over by a set
  mark, bid entry starts no later than a second mark, and signing starts with what is entered by 90 s before the
  end. Whatever is unfinished is omitted, never guessed. The marks are tuned from the first local runs.
- **Read-back before signing**: on the summary page the bid worker returns what the site shows per position and
  the total; code compares it with the plan and sends the worker back once if they differ.
- **The no_bid path**: entering a waiver has never been exercised. Step 4 runs it once locally (nothing counts
  with the scouting logins) so it is not first tried in a scored run.
- **Values from other sites in the bid form**: the grounding check refuses values a worker has not seen on its own
  site. Plan values are added to the bid session's `seen` text, as v1 already does for the TAN and email.
- **Generalisation check before every upload**: a script greps `agent/` for the public sites' names, hosts, labels
  seen while scouting and any value from `checks/`; a hit blocks the upload. The private final uses other sites.
- **Run-to-run noise**: the model is not deterministic. A change counts as an improvement only after two test runs
  agree; one run is a hint.
- **Shared quota**: test-run slots are shared with teammates. Local runs first; a sandbox run only when a local run
  ends with a signed bid.

## Decision I need at Step 3

When a position has no exactly matching active material, the rules call for `no_bid` (worth 75 points in such a
scenario, but a wrong `no_bid` in a bid scenario loses most of the score). My proposal: send `no_bid` only when the
ERP worker has read every candidate of that position's catalogue group and a second, thinking-on check agrees;
otherwise omit the position.

## Files

- Change: `agent/briefing.py`, `agent/agent.py`, `agent/agent.json`, `agent/submit.py`.
- New: `agent/evidence.py`, `agent/bidplan.py`, `agent/research.py`, `agent/tests/test_bidplan.py`.
- Reuse unchanged: `agent/worker.py`, `agent/browser_tools.py`, `agent/extract.py`, `agent/calc.py`,
  `agent/browsers.py`, `dev/test-run.sh`, `dev/run-local.sh`, `dev/dashboard.py`.
- `starter/` stays untouched and untracked.

## Verification

1. Unit tests: `(cd agent && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests)`.
2. Local run against the scouting sites: `dev/run-local.sh v2 "<what changed>"` (needs `atira models proxy`).
3. Sandbox: `dev/test-run.sh v2 "<what changed>"`, then the breakdown, `docs/dashboard.html` and the atira run
   tools for logs and model calls.
4. Fair play before any upload: `atira test-run ./agent --dry-run` and a read through `agent/` for site values.


If this plan is relevant to the current work and not already complete, continue working on it.
</system-reminder>

## atira
Atira Challenges: debug your team's agent system runs. Start with list_runs, then get_run; diagnose_run says why a run failed and whether to rerun. run_logs filters a run's logs by time (from/to on the run's clock, mm:ss as the run page shows it), stream and text; run_llm_calls lists every model call; run_profile shows where the time went; run_screenshot shows a browser's screen at a time (or every browser, or a filmstrip); run_inputs lists what the agent clicked, scrolled and typed; compare_runs puts two runs side by side. run_package shows the package a run or submission used (agent.json and its files) and saves it with out. test_run starts a test run from a folder; wait_for_run waits for it. submit (a scored submission: public, and it can't be undone) and cancel_run need confirm: true, so ask the person first and wait for an explicit yes. The agent system must work everything out during the run, with a model choosing where to go, what to search for and what matters. Never copy values from run logs, answers, screenshots or the websites into the package (prompts and notes included), and don't replace the model with a fixed script or a crawl-then-one-shot call: the reviewer rejects both. Rules at a glance: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Higgsfield
Recipe/setup slashes: get_preset_instructions before other workflows; unambiguous model slashes: models_explore; unknowns: resolve. For 3D scenes or location angles, first call get_preset_instructions with { preset: "/3d-jutsu" }. Character sheets require explicit requests. Bundled files: get_workflow_bundle_file. For AI Influencer chat creation, use ai_influencer_get_options for explicit traits, ai_influencer_list_presets for examples, or ai_influencer_get_settings with job_id for an existing sheet. ai_influencer_prepare returns design and price without generation. Preserve references and seed; use randomize=false for exact settings. Pass prepared params unchanged to ai_influencer_generate with max_credits at the quote or a lower user budget. Existing creation intent permits proceeding within budget; preview-only requests must stop after preparation. For explicit free-only intent, require known available free_gens_remaining and use_free_gens=true with max_credits=0; never fall back to credits. For variants, prepare each sheet and respect total count and aggregate budget. The generator opens an auto-updating widget for progress and the completed sheet. Wait with jobs_wait (timeout_seconds <= 15); do not duplicate the display with show_generation_by_ids or job_display unless explicitly requested. Offer Genjutsu animation afterward unless declined; require agreement and selection of the exact completed character before get_presets source=genjutsu category=genjutsu with initial_inputs.character_sheet=[{id:job_id,type:image_job}]. When unsure which model fits, call models_explore(action:'recommend') before calling a generate_* tool. Use virality_predictor when the user asks to predict video virality or analyze engagement, attention, audience response, retention risk, hook strength, or creative performance. For other existing-asset edits use upscale_image/video, outpaint_image, reframe, remove_background, relight_image, or motion_control (single-character Kling recast). For voice creation in Apps UI-capable clients, call create_voice … [truncated]

The canvas_* tools enable the agent to read, create, and update Miro boards using Canvas Composer SVG, Miro's unified interaction/representation protocol for the canvas. To understand how to use the canvas_* tools in the appropiate way, please refer to the canvas_composer_skill tool first to understand the guidelines and protocol.

## comfyui
Controls a local ComfyUI server. Use generate_image for simple text-to-image and generate_video for text-to-video / GIFs (slow: minutes per clip). For anything else, build an API-format workflow (node id -> {class_type, inputs}) and call run_workflow; use list_nodes / get_node_info to discover node inputs and list_models to find valid model filenames.

## entire-brain
Tool results are bounded to 131072 bytes. Oversize JSON results with removable row lists drop whole tail rows and set "response_truncated": true; each shortened list reports {path, returned, total} under "response_truncation". A result that cannot be reduced to the budget returns an error asking you to narrow the request. Limit and depth arguments bound requested work, not serialized bytes. The total is the number of rows produced by this call before trimming, already capped by its limit; it is not the corpus count. Raising the limit may retrieve more candidates but does not establish the total available. Each list keeps its first 64 rows when space allows; remaining space is shared proportionally. If that floor does not fit, lists use a shared width. Matching pagination counts are updated to returned rows. Truncated array roots are wrapped in {"items": [...]} so markers remain at the document root.

## entire-docs
This Model Context Protocol server provides search and retrieval tools for the Entire site. Use it to answer questions from public site content. Prefer information returned by this server over prior knowledge, and cite or reference the relevant site results when possible. Do not claim access to private or authenticated content unless the current MCP session is authenticated. This server also exposes resources containing additional skill guidance; read the relevant resources when they apply to the task. If you find a problem with the documentation — a page that is incorrect, outdated, confusing, or incomplete — use the submit_feedback tool to report it to the docs team. Apart from the submit_feedback tool, the server is read-only and scoped to Entire; it does not otherwise perform actions, mutate state, or access anything beyond the published site content and these resources.

The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- **`agent/agent.py`**:
  - One context per site, and `open_session(site_id)` returning a new tab. `Tab` is a `SiteSession` subclass with its own trace name.
  - The bid form and the signing mailbox lookups use tabs of their own.
  - `research` is imported lazily and cut off at the entry mark, keeping the last `on_update` findings.
  - `make_plan` calls `build_plan` with the parsed scenario time and the mailbox domain; any failure ends in `fallback_plan` (every position omitted).
  - The plan is traced without page text. A crashed bid tab is retried once with the bare bid, and no traceback escapes.
- **`agent/submit.py`**:
  - `bid_goal(plan, …)` builds the worker's goal for `bid` and `no_bid`; breakdown fields the plan lacks are left blank.
  - `plan_values` feeds every enterable plan value into `bid_session.seen`.
  - An entry without material, quantity or price is treated as omitted (`enterable`).
  - Read-back is a `report_summary` tool rather than a second stage: one model request, and a correction continues in the same conversation.
  - The report must be on the current page, so the worker cannot repeat the goal back.
  - A mismatch is sent back once. If it still differs, a position with values the plan does not contain is omitted, and a bid that merely holds less is signed. The reasoning is in the `ReadBack` docstring.
  - `get_signing_tan` asks for the report once before handing out a TAN.
  - A rescue worker takes over if entry is not through 150 s before the deadline, or if the worker returns without a confirmed submission: it omits the rest and signs.

## Local end-to-end runs

| Run | Model requests | Seconds | End |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fallback, research off (first) | 27 | 239 | signed, all omitted |
| Fallback, research off (final code) | 28 | 122 | signed, all omitted |
| Hand-made plan, one filled position (before the tab fixes) | 76+ | 775+ | not signed; stopped by me |
| Hand-made plan, one filled position | 47 | 150 | signed, 1 entered, 4 omitted |
| Hand-made `no_bid` | 23 | 104 | signed via the waiver option, no positions, total 0 |
| Full `agent.py` with research and `build_plan` | 178 | 563 | signed, all omitted |

- **First fallback run:** about 130 s of the 239 s were four hung model calls and one 30 s click timeout.
- **Failed hand-plan run:** the mailbox tab would not open for minutes, the bid session expired at the final click and the form was reset.
- **Full run:** research returned at the 417 s mark with one material, and the plan omitted every position for research gaps. An earlier full run reached the same point but I stopped it while it was stuck on the same mailbox problem.
- **Filled position:** the worker chose the material through the dependent selects by attributes, entered quantity, price, base price and lead time, and the read-back matched.

The read-back's mismatch branches (correction, omit, sign anyway) are covered by unit tests only; no live run produced a mismatch.

## The coordinator's three findings

1. **TAN lookup.** The traces showed three causes:
   - The view was taken while the mailbox page was still filling in: newest message selected, text missing. The reading pane loads after its check is passed, and the text after a second check inside the pane.
   - The worker then tried look-alike "open" controls, two of three leading away. One stalled the tab for 30 s and dropped the session; the next sign-in then hung on an element count with no timeout.
   - Opening and signing in to a mailbox tab sometimes took 7 to 25 s or more.

   Changes:
   - Every lookup gets its own tab at the mailbox start page, opened ahead of time and only reloaded when needed.
   - `let_finish` pauses and settles until two views agree before the worker's first look.
   - The lookup worker has a `wait_for_page()` tool and a goal that says not to search or use other controls.
   - Each try is capped at 45 s, with one replacement tab.
   - If the newest TAN is the one already returned, the bid worker is told to request a new one.

   Result: the last three signed runs each needed one TAN request and one lookup of 1 request in 3 to 4 s. The limit is 10, up from 8.
2. **Thinking.** The bid worker now runs with thinking off; `AGENT_ENTRY_THINKING=1` turns it on. The form with every position omitted took 81 to 103 s when no model call hung. I did not run a thinking-on comparison under the same conditions.
3. **Clean end.** A model error after a TAN was handed out is treated as the run being over: traced as `run_over`, no rescue, no retry. This path is not exercised locally, because the scouting run never revokes the token.

## Time-budget constants (`agent.py`)

- Research ends at `RESEARCH_SHARE` 0.45 of the run, capped at `RESEARCH_MAX_SECONDS` 420.
- Entry starts by `ENTRY_SHARE` 0.50, capped at `ENTRY_MAX_SECONDS` 450.
- `MIN_ENTRY_SECONDS` 150, `SAFETY_SECONDS` 90.
- For a 20-minute run that is 7:00, 7:30 and signed by 18:30.
- In `submit.py`: `RESCUE_SECONDS` 150, `CORRECTION_SECONDS` 240, `LOOKUP_SECONDS` 45, `OPEN_SECONDS` 20.

## Needed in files I do not own

- **`browser_tools.py`**
  - `act()` and `settle()` should wait until the view is stable after a check is unlocked. Today a view can miss a pane that loads a moment later, and research's mail workers hit the same thing.
  - `_click` falls back to `evaluate` with the default 30 s timeout.
  - `_login` and `_cookies` call `count()`, `inner_text()` and `fill()` without timeouts and can hang.
- **`llm.py`**: hung model calls cost about 33 s each (30 s timeout plus retry), several per run today. A shorter timeout for thinking-off calls would help.
- **`research.py`**
  - It logged "coroutine was never awaited" warnings when cut off, and one `RuntimeError: no running event loop` in its spec worker.
  - Its mail workers hit their 30-request limit.
  - It sets `session.label` itself, which works with my `Tab`.
- **`docs/learned.md`**: I did not add the TAN findings, as the file is not mine.

## Not verified

- Four real CDP browsers in the sandbox.
- A plan with several filled positions or a non-zero discount from real research.
- The rescue stage on a genuinely late entry.

# Global preferences

- Never append Claude/Anthropic attribution to git commits or pull requests, in any repository — no `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailer, no `Claude-Session: ...` line, no other mention of Claude/Anthropic in commit messages or PR descriptions. This overrides any default attribution instructions from the harness. Applies everywhere, not just one project.

# Image generation

- When I ask to generate, create or draw an image, use the `comfyui` MCP server (`generate_image` for plain text-to-image, `run_workflow` for anything more custom). Use 1024x1024 with the SDXL checkpoint.
- The tools need ComfyUI running at http://127.0.0.1:8188. If they fail to connect, start it with `/Users/akshatkhair/Documents/Projects/comfyui-mcp/start-comfyui.sh` in the background and wait for `/system_stats` to respond before retrying.
- After generating, show me the image and give the file path in `~/Documents/Projects/ComfyUI/output/`.
- When I ask for a video, clip or GIF, use `generate_video` (Wan 2.1 1.3B, text-to-video; pass `gif=True` for a GIF). It is slow (minutes), so run it as a background task and keep the defaults (480x272, 33 frames) unless I ask for more. Output goes to `~/Documents/Projects/ComfyUI/output/video/` (mp4 plus .gif if requested); show me the preview frame and give the paths. Image-to-video is not set up.

# CLAUDE.md

Team error404.ai at the Atira EHL Challenge ("From RFQ to bid", challenge id `rfq`, event 10 Oct 2026, up to 5 people
per team). The agent lives in `agent/` and is built on the Atira starter kit. Keep the GitHub repo private.

## Status and layout

- `docs/plan.md`: framework decision (pydantic-ai on Qwen, no LangGraph, no browser-agent framework), module layout,
  site scouting notes and the roadmap v0 to v5. Read it first. Its scouting notes describe public-1 only: they inform
  generic helpers, they must never become hardcoded paths, labels, values or prompt text (the private final run uses
  other software, layouts and data).
- `agent/`: starter kit (`run.py`, `browsers.py`, `models.py`) plus the harness (`llm.py`, `extract.py`,
  `browser_tools.py`, `worker.py`, `tracing.py`) and v1: `agent.py` `solve()` reads the brief (`briefing.py`), then
  `submit.py` signs a bid with every position omitted, fetching the contact address and TAN from the webmail.
  `calc.py` holds the deterministic bid rules (tested, not wired in yet). `agent.json` asks for 2 browsers.
- `dev/smoke.py`: the v0 check (one worker per site logs in and reads a page). From the repo root:
  `eval "$(atira scout --env)"; HEADLESS=1 uv run --project agent python dev/smoke.py [siteId ...]`
- Next: v2 to v4 for field points (research workers for spec, ERP, tender Q&A and mail, wired into `calc.py`). Use
  `git status` and `atira status` for the current state; do not trust dated numbers in this file.

## Tracking runs

Record every test run and submission; they go to `experiments/runs.jsonl` (append-only, `merge=union`, committed with
the change it measured). Local runs go to `experiments/local-runs.jsonl` (gitignored). `python3 dev/track.py report`
renders both to `docs/experiments.md` (gitignored). From the repo root:

```sh
dev/test-run.sh v1 "what changed" [experiment]    # sandbox test run, followed to the end, score recorded
dev/run-local.sh v1 "what changed" [experiment]   # local, headless; needs `atira models proxy`
python3 dev/track.py platform <sub_id> --version v1 --experiment NAME --note "..."   # after `atira submit`
```

`version` is the base being measured (v1, v2, ...); `experiment` names what a run varies on top of it (e.g.
`thinking-off-forms`, `model-<name>`, `4-browsers`), so variants of one version compare side by side. Environment
overrides (`AGENT_*`, `LLM_*`, `THINKING*`, `MAX_STEPS*`) are recorded, with secrets redacted. `atira test-run`
uploads untracked files too, so the recorded commit is a pointer; `atira package <id>` shows the exact upload.
When a run taught something (a failure mode, a speed-up, a score change), add a bullet to `docs/learned.md`. Notes
never contain credentials or values copied from the sites.

## Platform docs (source of truth; re-read, they change)

Base `https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai`. Public pages (home, start, challenge, leaderboard, team profiles) are also
Markdown via `.md`; docs are `/docs/<name>.md`.

- `/start.md`, `/challenges/rfq.md` (29 bid rules, answer schema), `/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md`
- `/docs/fair-play.md`, `scoring.md`, `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `building-an-agent.md`, `cli.md`, `api.md`,
  `mcp.md`, `faq.md`, `demo-day.md`; `/openapi.json`, `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt` (all docs in one file)
- Announcements need a token: `curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)" https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/v1/announcements`
- Submission deadline and prizes are not in the docs: ask the organizers. Demo day: best teams run live on stage, so
  keep a one-line start command (`atira test-run ./agent`) and a fallback recording.

The scouting logins are deliberately NOT stored here: run `atira scout`. Never write them, or anything copied from
the sites, into code, prompts, fixtures, notes or fallbacks.

## Fair play (an AI reviewer rejects or flags these)

- No hardcoded scenario values (tender refs, material numbers, prices, discounts, logins, TANs), not even as defaults,
  fallbacks or in prompts. Facts the brief states for every scenario (e.g. the sales director's mailbox) are fine.
- No pre-solving, by you or an AI assistant, put into the package. Hand-derived expectations stay outside `agent/`.
- Must be agentic: a model chooses where to go, what to search and what matters. Rejected: a fixed click path (model
  unused or only a fallback), or a crawler/helper that gathers all evidence before model-directed investigation.
  Allowed helpers: parse a page or document the model chose, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate,
  validate, retry, fill forms. Several agents and parallel browsers are fine.
- Only the platform API, the four sites and the model proxy; no local models; no own browsers in the sandbox (use the
  provided 1 to 4, tabs and contexts are free).
- Do not write notes meant to steer the reviewer. Outcomes: passed; flagged (runs, but hidden from the leaderboard
  until an organizer passes it); rejected (no runs).

## The task and its traps

One signed bid, entered in the tender portal's configurator and signed with a TAN from the webmail. Site ids are
public-1 names; the private set renames and re-splits sites, so never branch code on siteId, URL or layout.

| Site | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| Tender portal | Tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A (the hub: quantity changes, withdrawals, scoped spec amendments, Konditionsgruppe, packaging, commitment and setup-pool keys), configurator |
| Supplier portal | Buyer's spec and revisions (oldest shown first; use the one marked current) |
| ERP | Materials and status, stock, lead times, price conditions with validity and scales, pieces per carton, allocation mass |
| Webmail | Director's discount approval, TAN, authority mails (look-alikes, superseded, archive) |

Read all 29 rules in `challenges/rfq.md` before writing prompts or tools. Highest-impact traps:

- **Authority and time (21):** per key, the latest record dated no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender
  reference, from the right sender (technik, logistik, finanzen, kalkulation + bidder mailbox domain). Future-dated and
  unrelated records never apply; a failed condition does not revive an older record.
- **no_bid (3, 8, 16):** if any position has no exactly matching active material (after amendments and the "nutzbarer
  Weg" derivation, rule 20), send `no_bid`, no positions, `total_net` 0 (schema still requires `discount_percent`; a
  conditional approval means 0 %). Omitting positions is not a substitute (rule 9).
- **Sign and submit:** saving alone scores nothing. Partial bids use "Position auslassen" and are still signed.
- **Per position vs per material:** price scales per position; stock pooled per material (15); delivery commitments
  per position, only if the material matches and pooled demand is within the inclusive ceiling (24).
- **Rounding:** HALF_UP, at the steps the rules name: FX-converted base price to cents (22), discount threshold and
  bonus aggregate to cents (16, 26), then the final unit price once from unrounded per-piece components (27).
  Breakdown fields are reports, not inputs. Bonus split: largest remainders (26); setup pool: the cent-allocation rule
  stated in the Ruestpools mail (25).
- **Reporting:** `surcharge_per_unit` is before discount and covers mass surcharge plus ordinary and allocated setup;
  setup and packaging are never discounted; blank = unanswered, `0.00` = known zero; `rebate_total` is per position.
- **Conditional discount (16):** threshold uses undiscounted scale prices, no surcharge or setup, inclusive; on failure
  0 %, never an older approval. Metal index: the rate whose window contains the scenario date (28).
- Positions are matched by number; extras or duplicates cost one position's share; money is compared to the cent.

## Runs, ranking, winning

Details live in `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `scoring.md`, `faq.md`. What bites:

- Test run (`atira test-run ./agent --follow`): 2 h, public data, shows per-part points, never on the leaderboard.
  Scored (`atira submit ./agent`): AI review, then one 20-minute run, one submission in flight per team (else 429).
- Time runs from the start of the run command to the accepted answer. 202 is final (even if wrong); 400 lists issues
  and the clock keeps running; validate against `answer_schema` first. Submit about 90 s before `expires_at` (the kit's

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

You have a persistent file-based memory at `/Users/akshatkhair/.claude/projects/-Users-akshatkhair-Documents-Projects-error404ai-ehl-finals/memory/`. When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

# Finishing work
Ending your turn means your work stops there until asked to continue, and you should not stop unless needed. Please avoid stopping while work the user asked for is still owed. Stopping before the task is complete can rarely be merited, i.e. when the task can't move forward without user input, or where the blocker is deliberate and should not be worked past. This adds to the Memory section and takes precedence over it. The rules about saving apply only if this session has a directory for saving memories.

Save only what is applicable and durable:
applicable: it would directly change your behavior in future sessions, such as an approach the user corrected or steered you away from, or a standing preference they expressed. Not ambient code context or state.
durable: it applies to multiple future sessions and tasks, not just this one. Not transient task plans or status. If you are uncertain whether something is durable, assume it is not and do not save it.

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
